arguments.summary: A critical credential compromise incident was detected in the Finance OU, originating from external IP 185.220.101.42. The attacker conducted reconnaissance via port scanning from a compromised internal host (WS-IT-101), then performed pass-the-hash attacks to compromise all 23 accounts in the Finance department. Despite detection, immediate containment actions (credential revocation, firewall blocking) were denied due to policy enforcement, indicating a gap in incident response authorization protocols.

timeline.description: External IP 185.220.101.42 scanned internal host WS-IT-101 (Ubuntu 24.04 LTS), triggering IDS alert for Nmap SYN scan.
Successful authentication from WS-IT-101 to domain controller as CORP\helpdesk, indicating potential credential compromise.
Lateral movement detected: 23 successful authentications linked to Finance OU users from compromised session.
SOC analyst identified pass-the-hash attack pattern and requested bulk credential revocation and firewall block.
Containment actions denied by policy system; incident escalated due to inability to execute critical response steps.

arguments.rule_content:
title: Multiple Authentication Success from Single Host to High-Value OU
id: 9a3f7d21-4b6e-4a1a-8c1a-0e7b5f5c5d5a
description: Detects multiple successful authentications from a single source host to user accounts within a high-value organizational unit (e.g., Finance), indicative of pass-the-hash or credential dumping.
status: experimental
author: SOC Team
logsource:
  category: authentication
  product: windows
  service: security
detection:
  selection:
    EventID: 4624
    LogonType: 3
    TargetUserName|endswith: '@finance.corp.local'
  group_by:
    - SourceHostname
  condition: selection | count(TargetUserName) by SourceHostname > 20
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate bulk operations by administrators
level: critical
